blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built from provincial and municipal pages named under Sources, read November 1, 2026.
These BC rules apply to every townhome purchase on this site, whichever neighbourhood it is in. They are written once here; each community page covers only what is specific to that community.
Presales (REDMA)

a presale buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18, deposits held in trust) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21) — the frame for Kings Crossing and any other developer sale surfacing in this band.
Depreciation reports

since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote. CRF minimum: since Nov 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund. Rental-restriction bylaws are void: since Nov 24, 2022, no BC strata residential rental-restriction bylaw is valid; short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw. Age bylaws: only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1, 123.2); lower ages have been invalid since Nov 24, 2022, and the rule binds residents, not owners.
Rental-restriction bylaws are void

Short-term rentals are prohibited in Pitt Meadows at the city layer — short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use in the City's Zoning Bylaw, per the City's zoning bylaw amendments staff report; the provincial voiding does not create a short-term rental right here. Do not price any South Meadows home on short-term-rental income.
Age bylaws

only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023 for a younger spouse/partner, live-in caregivers, legacy residents and defined children).
Taxes and rebates

PTT is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million; a page row reading "Over $3M — 5%" is a compression of the 3% tier plus that further 2% — the tier math governs. A purchase in this band pays only the 1% and 2% tiers. Worked examples, inputs stated: (1) an $800,000 townhouse at the band ceiling, no exemption = 1% × $200,000 ($2,000) + 2% × $600,000 ($12,000) = $14,000. (2) a $600,000 townhouse, no exemption = $2,000 + 2% × $400,000 ($8,000) = $10,000; a qualifying first-time buyer on the same $600,000 purchase, exempt on the first $500,000, pays 2% × $100,000 = $2,000 on those inputs. FTHB GST rebate — Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 (100% of GST to $1M, maximum $50,000, phasing to $1.5M, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031); New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350K–$450K; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%. 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales — in this band that means developer sales (for example any remaining developer unit at Viva) and presale contracts, not the resale stock.
Fee-simple contrast

A fee-simple (non-strata) townhouse or row house has no strata corporation, no Form B, and no strata fees — the buyer deals with municipal rules and any covenants or homeowners-association terms on title only. No fee-simple townhouse complex is verified in Delta Manor, so any Ladner listing marketed as "freehold, no strata" needs its title checked to prove the non-strata claim.
Form B diligence

A buyer of a strata townhouse is entitled to an Information Certificate (Form B) under s. 59 of the Strata Property Act, to be provided within seven days of request; the fee is capped at $35 plus up to 25 cents per page for paper copies. The Form B states the monthly strata fee, money the owner owes the strata, any special levies approved but not yet due, the contingency reserve fund (CRF) balance, the strata's insurance, its rules, its current budget and financial statement, any Rental Disclosure Statement, and the current depreciation report attached (BC Government, strata Forms information: Strata Property Act, s. 59).
Rentals

Rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 for strata property; short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw, and in Chilliwack short-term rental OPERATIONS are separately regulated by the City under Short-Term Rental Bylaw 2021, No. 5141 (adopted November 24, 2021, which repealed the former Bed and Breakfast Bylaw 2003, No. 2968) — confirm the property can be licensed under it before valuing any STR income.
PTT

general rates 1% of fair market value up to and including $200,000; 2% of the portion greater than $200,000 and up to and including $2,000,000; 3% of the portion greater than $2,000,000. Worked anchors: $700K → $12,000; $1.0M → $18,000; $1.2M → $22,000; $1.5M → $28,000. Newly built home exemption: full threshold $1,100,000, phasing out over the $50,000 range above it and eliminated at $1,150,000.
New Housing Rebate

36% / maximum $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000 phase-out. Exemptions: first-time buyers full on first $500,000 at ≤$835,000, phasing to $860,000; newly built full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000. HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%. The Vancouver Empty Homes Tax does not apply — Surrey is not Vancouver.
Age

Only 55+ age bylaws are valid since November 24, 2022 (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 and Regulation 7.01; spouse/caregiver/legacy exemptions including the May 1, 2023 expansion; a 45+ bylaw is void and does not convert to 55+).
FTHB GST rebate (new housing only)

Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 — March 13 governs; secondary sources' March 12 is rejected, CRA governs. Together with the GST/HST new housing rebate it provides 100% of the GST (or federal part of the HST) on a newly constructed or substantially renovated home valued up to $1,000,000, is gradually reduced between $1,000,000 and $1,500,000 (CRA's wording — a page's $1.25M straight-line phase-out row is not verified as a mechanism), and is not available at $1,500,000 or more — maximum $50,000. Eligibility turns on a builder agreement entered into on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031 (owner-built construction beginning on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031), construction begun before 2031 and substantially completed before 2036, and the buyer being at least 18, a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and a first-time buyer under the four-calendar-year look-back.

blocks.text: BC Townhome Buying Rules: streets and boundaries

items.t: The boundary that matters on this page is which level of government sets which rule. The Strata Property Act, the Home Buyer Rescission Period and Property Transfer Tax (PTT) are provincial; Goods and Services Tax (GST) on new homes is federal; secondary-suite and parking rules are municipal; and pet, smoking and alteration rules for a specific complex are set by that strata corporation's own bylaws.

A townhouse is usually a strata lot: the Province states strata housing includes townhouses, and that you cannot tell by looking whether a townhouse is strata-titled or a non-strata rowhouse — the legal test is whether a strata plan was filed at the Land Title Office.
Where a rule below is municipal, it differs by city; where it is provincial or federal, it applies the same way in every BC municipality.

blocks.text: BC Townhome Buying Rules: the housing stock

items.t: Three townhome forms meet different rules. A standard (building) strata townhome is shown on the strata plan, so the strata corporation insures the building; a bare-land strata townhome lot is defined by survey markers, not by the house's walls, and the house on it is not shown on the plan.

In a bare-land strata (called a "strata subdivision"), the strata plan is filed before homes are built, the lot is essentially a plot of land, and common property can include roads, streetlights, septic systems and utility lines running under individual lots.

blocks.text: BC Townhome Buying Rules: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Strata basics: a strata corporation is created when a strata plan is filed at the Land Title Office; owners own their strata lot individually and own the common property together as the strata corporation.

Rental restrictions are gone: as of November 24, 2022, no strata corporation in British Columbia may have a residential rental-restriction bylaw, and all such bylaws are invalid — although short-term rental bylaws are still allowed.

Age restrictions are narrowed the same way: since November 24, 2022 a strata may only restrict age to 55 years or older, with exemptions added May 1, 2023 for caregivers, previous residents, children (including adult children) and younger spouses or partners.

Depreciation reports are now mandatory on a cycle: every strata corporation with five or more strata lots, including bare-land stratas, must obtain one every five years, and owners may no longer defer it by an annual three-quarter vote.

Insurance is mandatory for every strata corporation, including bare-land developments with townhouses: the Strata Property Act requires property and liability insurance, and the Province advises owners to carry their own policy for contents, upgrades and liability because the strata policy is not homeowner insurance.

Municipal suite rules sit on top of strata rules: for example, the Township of Langley zoning bylaw definition allows one secondary suite per principal dwelling unit, including in a townhouse, capped at 120 square metres — the city you buy in sets its own figure, so check that city's bylaw, not a provincial page.

blocks.text: BC Townhome Buying Rules: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: A depreciation report projects 30 years ahead: the Province states it inventories the strata's common property and assets and projects maintenance, repair and replacement costs over a 30-year span, including roads and amenities in bare-land stratas.

Timing trap for older complexes: a strata corporation with no depreciation report, or one received before December 31, 2020, in Metro Vancouver or the Fraser Valley had to obtain a new report by July 1, 2026 under the strengthened July 1, 2024 regulations.
From July 1, 2027, owner developers must contribute toward a new strata's first depreciation report: a minimum of $5,000 plus $200 per strata lot, to a maximum of $30,000.

Earthquake coverage is optional, not mandatory: the Province states strata corporations are not required to buy earthquake insurance because earthquake is not a listed peril in the regulation, but advises corporations in earthquake-prone areas to consider it, noting earthquake deductibles are typically a percentage of full replacement value.

Old bylaw packages still print dead rules: a rental cap or a 19-plus age bylaw in a townhome complex's documents is invalid under the November 24, 2022 changes even if the strata never reprinted its bylaws.

The long-standing GST/HST New Housing Rebate is small at BC prices: the CRA guide states it is generally 36 percent of the GST paid, to a maximum of $6,300, reducing between $350,000 and $450,000 of value and unavailable at $450,000 or more — separate from the first-time buyer rebate.

blocks.text: BC Townhome Buying Rules: development and new projects

items.t: No single development belongs to this province-wide topic page; project-level entries are carried on the neighbourhood and city pages where the project sits.

Rule changes acting like a development pipeline: the strengthened depreciation-report regulations took effect July 1, 2024, and the owner-developer contribution toward first reports for new stratas begins July 1, 2027. Status: in force / scheduled as stated (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: BC Townhome Buying Rules: costs and taxes

items.t: Property Transfer Tax general rates are charged on fair market value at registration: 1 percent on the first $200,000, 2 percent on the portion to $2,000,000 and 3 percent above that, with a further 2 percent on the residential portion above $3,000,000 on the Province's calculator before closing.
The rescission fee is a closing cost if you use it: 0.25 percent of the purchase price, paid to the seller, under the Home Buyer Rescission Period.
The Form B fee is capped provincially at $35 plus up to 25 cents per page for copying.

blocks.text: BC Townhome Buying Rules: getting around

items.t: This is a topic page, not a place: the "getting around" step is getting the right document from the right office. Title and the strata plan itself come from the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia (LTSA), because a strata corporation exists only once its plan is filed at the Land Title Office.
Strata disclosure (Form B, budget, rules, depreciation report) comes from the strata corporation, which must answer a Form B request within 7 days.

Tax questions split by level: PTT exemptions are claimed on the provincial Property Transfer Tax return at registration, while GST rebates are claimed from the Canada Revenue Agency or credited by the builder.

blocks.text: BC Townhome Buying Rules: risks and due diligence

items.t: Read the depreciation report before subject removal: it is the document that shows what common property the strata must repair and what the projected costs are over 30 years, and stratas with four or fewer lots are exempt from obtaining one — a gap to notice on a small townhome complex.
Check the strata's insurance summary on the Form B: since 2023 the Form B must summarize strata corporation insurance, and the deductible the owners could face is part of that disclosure.

Confirm the plan type on the strata plan itself: if the words "bare land strata" do not appear and houses are shown on the plan, it is a building strata, and the strata corporation's insurance and repair duties cover the buildings shown.

Municipal rules can block a suite the strata allows, and strata bylaws can block uses the city allows; a townhome buyer needs both answers, from the city's zoning bylaw and the strata's filed bylaws, before counting on rental or suite income.

blocks.text: What is not confirmed about BC Townhome Buying Rules

items.t: Whether a specific townhome complex allows pets, and in what number or size: that is set by each strata corporation's own bylaws and no provincial page states it — read the filed bylaws for the complex.
A single provincial figure for strata insurance deductible amounts: deductibles are set policy by policy; only the duty to insure and to summarize it on the Form B are stated provincially.

items.t: Mount Currie Real Estate Guide

faq.a: It varies by complex and the published record is listing copy, not bylaws: a current Rossmoor listing records "Cats OK" and states pets are welcome, and an Ashbrook Place listing calls the complex "petfriendly." Henley Estate and Wembley Estates pet positions: Not confirmed. Confirm the registered pet bylaw for the specific complex on the Form B before relying on any of it.

faq.q: New-build GST — do I get it back?
faq.a: All four counted complexes are resale stock, so GST does not apply to the purchase itself. On a new townhouse elsewhere, 5% GST applies; the FTHB GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026) returns 100% of GST to $1M (max $50,000, phasing to $1.5M) for qualifying first-time buyers with agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031, and the older New Housing Rebate returns 36% to a $6,300 maximum in the $350K–$450K band.

faq.q: How do I get downtown without a car?
faq.a: Blue Bus route 254 (British Properties) serves the properties from Park Royal Exchange, and route 250 on Marine Drive below the hillside runs between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge. Canterbury is otherwise a drive-to-everything address — price it as one.

faq.q: Strata or non-strata — which townhouse am I actually looking at in Sullivan Station?
faq.a: No fee-simple townhouse complex was verified. Check the Title to Land field before assuming — and note the one non-strata trap by name: Sullivan Mews is a membership purchase in East Newton, not a Sullivan Station strata.

faq.q: How does a BC foreclosure start?
faq.a: By petition in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under Rule 21-7(1); everyone whose interest in the property is sought to be extinguished must be made a respondent, and the petitioner must serve the court's foreclosure information notice, Form 125, with the petition. Rule 21-7 sets out no demand step before the petition.

faq.q: Can someone outbid my accepted offer?
faq.a: In Surrey's deep attached market, assume other buyers are watching the same listing.

faq.q: Do I pay GST on a townhome?
faq.a: Only if it is new or substantially renovated. The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) taxes new homes bought from a builder and rebates part of the GST through the GST/HST New Housing Rebate; a resale townhome carries no GST. Eligible first-time buyers can now recover 100 percent of the GST on a new home valued at or under $1 million, reducing to zero at $1.5 million.

faq.q: Can I change my mind after my offer is accepted?
faq.a: Yes, for three business days. British Columbia Financial Services Authority (BCFSA) explains the Home Buyer Rescission Period under the Property Law Act: in force January 3, 2023, it lets a buyer rescind a contract for residential real property, including a residential strata lot, up to three business days after acceptance, on payment of 0.25 percent of the price to the seller, and it cannot be waived.

faq.q: What is a Form B and how fast must the strata produce it?
faq.a: The Form B (Information Certificate) is the strata corporation's disclosure about the specific lot and corporation, and a buyer may request one. The Province states the strata must provide it within 7 days of a request, may charge at most $35 plus up to 25 cents per page, and since 2023 Form Bs must also include summaries of the strata's insurance and electrical planning reports.

faq.q: Does a new townhome avoid Property Transfer Tax?
faq.a: It can. The Province's newly built home exemption fully eliminates PTT on a qualifying principal-residence purchase at a fair market value of $1,100,000 or less for registrations on or after April 1, 2024, and phases out completely at $1,150,000. Foreign entities and taxable trustees are not eligible, and the buyer claims it on the PTT return using exemption code 49.
